result.title: PRC4D: Physical Relation-Constrained Persistent 4D Reconstruction
result.summary: A faithful 4D reconstruction should capture both the shape and motion of objects, even when they disappear from view. Existing methods preserve previously observed geometry and extend motion through occlusion using local spatial and motion associations. However, treating short-term contact or shared motion as sufficient evidence of persistent rigidity can introduce incorrect motion constraints and distort overall reconstruction. To address this limitation, we present PRC4D, a physical relation-constrained framework that identifies reliable rigid relations and uses them to maintain spatial consistency through occlusion. PRC4D combines 3D contact and relative motion consistency with sequence-level verification to distinguish persistent couplings from transient interactions. The resulting graph guides observed-pose refinement and motion propagation from visible to occluded components without altering reconstructed geometry. Experiments on diverse real-world multi-object sequences and controlled occlusion simulations demonstrate improved reconstruction accuracy, reduced relative pose errors, and more consistent object configurations under changing visibility.

AI.brief_summary: PRC4D 提出物理关系约束的持久 4D 重建框架：结合 3D 接触与相对运动一致性，并用序列级验证区分持久刚体耦合与瞬时交互，据此构建关系图来精化观测位姿并在遮挡时把运动传播到不可见部件。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「序列级验证持久耦合 vs. 瞬时接触」并用关系图约束状态传播的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中跨时刻维持实体关系状态、筛除误导性视觉证据的问题，但该方法属几何重建管线，可迁移性需读原文判断。
